record.paper_title: Open Problems in Partial Differential Equations Arising from Fluid Dynamics
record.original_question: For the three-dimensional incompressible Euler equations, do smooth solutions of the Cauchy problem break down in finite time? Equivalently, can vorticity stretching and accumulation create a finite-time singularity from smooth initial data, or does global smooth well-posedness persist?

evidence.quote: Well-posedness of the Cauchy problem for the incompressible Euler equations. Do smooth solutions to the 3-dimensional incompressible Euler equations break down in finite time?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Cauchy problem for the three-dimensional incompressible Euler equations on $\mathbb{R}^3$:
$$\partial_t u + (u\cdot
abla)u + 
abla p = 0, \qquad 
abla\cdot u = 0, \qquad u(\cdot,0)=u_0,$$
where $u:\mathbb{R}^3	imes[0,T)	o\mathbb{R}^3$ is the velocity field and $p:\mathbb{R}^3	imes[0,T)	o\mathbb{R}$ is the pressure. Assume the initial datum $u_0$ is smooth (e.g., $u_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3)\cap L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$ or in a Schwartz class), divergence-free, and has finite energy.

Determine whether there exists such an initial datum $u_0$ for which the corresponding classical solution $u$ ceases to be smooth in finite time; equivalently, decide whether vorticity stretching and accumulation (with vorticity $\omega=
abla	imes u$ satisfying $\partial_t\omega+(u\cdot
abla)\omega=(\omega\cdot
abla)u$) can drive $\int_0^{T^*}\|\omega(\cdot,t)\|_{L^\infty}\,dt=\infty$ for some finite $T^*<\infty$ (by the Beale–Kato–Majda criterion), or whether instead every smooth, finite-energy initial datum yields a globally smooth solution.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem on the whole space $\mathbb{R}^3$ with smooth finite-energy initial data remains open. Significant progress has been made: Elgindi (2021) proved finite-time singularity formation for $C^{1,\alpha}$ velocities, and Chen–Hou (2025, PNAS) gave a computer-assisted proof of finite-time, nearly self-similar blowup for 3D axisymmetric Euler in a smooth bounded domain with smooth initial data. The general smooth-data case on $\mathbb{R}^3$ without boundary is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Singularity formation in 3D Euler equations with smooth initial data and boundary
status_evidence.snippet: Computer-assisted proof of finite-time nearly self-similar blowup for 3D axisymmetric Euler in a smooth bounded domain with smooth initial data.
status_evidence.claim: Blow-up established with smooth data in the presence of a boundary; the boundary-free smooth case remains open.

status_evidence.title: Finite Time Singularities to the 3D Incompressible Euler Equations for Solutions in C^∞(R^3∖{0})∩C^{1,α}∩L^2
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of finite-time singularity for solutions with only C^{1,α} regularity at one point.
status_evidence.claim: Singularity established for C^{1,α} regularity class; not for fully smooth data on R^3.

status_evidence.title: Potential Singularity of the 3D Euler Equations in the Interior Domain
status_evidence.snippet: Numerical evidence for potential singularity formation.
status_evidence.claim: Numerical, not yet a proof for smooth data in free space.
